findings.evidence: The OR clause treats an attacker-supplied x-admin: yes header as sufficient for admin, bypassing authenticated identity and exposing invoices.
Only the first 8 hex characters (16 bits) of the HMAC are checked with startsWith, allowing a brute-forced prefix to pass and using a non-constant-time comparison.
tenantId and invoiceId are concatenated into a quoted SQL literal, so a quote in either value can alter the WHERE clause and disclose other tenants' invoices.
requestCount > 6 returns false when requestCount is 6, so the sixth request is not blocked as required.
